name: _test_string_default
description: Representative ATen signature (not exclusive): aten::_test_string_default(Tensor dummy, str a="\"\'\\", str b="\"\'\\") -> Tensor. That signature is representative only and is not an exclusive ABI: the original Gems pytest owns the full contract, including overload selection, positional and keyword spellings of the two optional strings, returns and return identity, aliasing, mutation and every error case, so tests must not be narrowed to this one signature. Registered schema strings listed verbatim: aten::_test_string_default(Tensor dummy, str a="\"\'\\", str b="\"\'\\") -> Tensor. Semantics: the operator takes one tensor operand dummy plus two optional strings a and b, each of which must equal the ATen schema default whose raw characters are double-quote, apostrophe and backslash; non-JSON ATen defaults cannot be carried literally, so the schema's escaped spelling is retained verbatim above and the same stable three-character value is used as the default of both optional parameters. Any other default value, a non-string or unknown keyword argument, or a non-tensor operand is rejected, while a None operand is accepted and returned unchanged. The operator validates the strings and hands dummy back untouched, so the result equals the operand exactly and is the same object, with shape, stride, storage_offset, dtype, layout, device, lazy conjugate and negate bits and requires_grad preserved. The pytest additionally covers empty, scalar, strided, offset-window, expanded, lazily conjugated and lazily negated operands, unchanged upstream gradients through backward, and writes through the result being visible in the operand. The representative overload declares no mutation or argument aliases and has exactly one tensor return, counted as one logical output.
